newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's red chip index up on asset injection hopes.
newsitem.headline: HK's red chip index up on asset injection hopes.

text.p: Hong Kong's red chip index edged ahead on Tuesday, outperforming the Hang Seng Index after a boost from asset injection stories and positive pre-handover sentiment, brokers and analysts said.
"The red chips are still being boosted by the news that China Everbright-IHD will acquire a 20 percent stake in Everbright Bank of China," said Jeffrey Lin, vice president at Merrill Lynch.
The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index, which was launched on Monday, gained 20.27 points, or 0.71 percent, to close at 2,887.59 but was off the day's high of 2,918.87.
The blue chip Hang Seng Index lost 87.45 points, or 0.61 percent, to close at 14,307.15.
"The launch of the index gave an excuse to buy (red chips)," said Janet Gillies, sales director at OCBC Securities. "Good handover news outweighed bad today."
China regains sovereignty over Hong Kong on July 1.
Constituents of the red chip index for China-related stocks topped the market's most active list, with turnover in index heavyweight Guangdong Investment leading the field.

The share closed just HK$0.10 higher at HK$10.35 on heavy trade of HK$764.55 million. The company said on Tuesday it would take up 44 million of the 88 million new shares placed by its subsidiary Guangdong Tannery Ltd.

Brokers said the international reputation of the Hang Seng Index and other indices compiled by HSI Services meant this red chip index would become the focus of market attention rather than other red chip indices.
But criticism of the make-up of the index continued.
"The index is not yet representative," said a broker at Peregrine. "(The omission of) China Everbright-IHD Pacific is the biggest disappointment, chiefly because it is so big."
China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd, following the placement of 175 million new shares recently, had a market capitalisation of about HK$13 billion.

The largest stock in the index in terms of market capitalisation, China Resources Enterprise Ltd, had a total market value of HK$41.53 billion as at Tuesday's closing price of HK$27.70, a HK$.05 gain on the day.

On the other hand, the Shougang group was included and these companies were unlikely to get the same sort of support from the parent company, particularly in the way of asset injections as the Everbright group were, the broker said.

Shougang Concord Century Holdings Ltd, Shougang Concord Technology Holdings Ltd and Shougang Concord International Enterprises Co Ltd have been relatively inactive, since former chairman Zhou Peifang was found guilty of corruption by Beijing courts.

"The five biggest stocks, China Resources, Shanghai Industrial, China Overseas, GDI (Guangdong Investment) and COSCO (Pacific Ltd), account for more than 50 percent of the index, so the index is going to reflect the performance of these stocks, but they are not an accurate reflection of the sector," said Merrill Lynch's Lin.
His chief criticism was the omission of Beijing Enterprises.
"Beijing Enterprises is representative of other upcoming window companies," said Lin.
Analysts believe Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd, as the only listed investment vehicle of the Beijing Municipal government, is a major conglomerate in the making.
Its Hong Kong listing represented a window for foreign investors to take a stake in the growth of the Beijing economy and a means for Beijing enterprises to tap overseas capital.
Several other commercial entities set up by municipal and provincial governments in China are to be brought to the Hong Kong market in the second half of the year.
Beijing Enterprises closed HK$0.50 lower at HK$47.90.
